thesis: Armageddon turns a lead on the battlefield into a lock on future development, making it less a comeback card than a way to freeze an advantage.

competitiveTimeline.significance: Its tournament story runs through white weenie, Erhnam-Geddon, prison, and tempo decks that used a modest board lead to end the opponent's ability to participate.

playbook.role: Cast it only when your creatures, artifacts, or planeswalkers leave you ahead after every land disappears. Mana creatures and artifact mana convert the apparent symmetry into continued development.

counterplay.directAnswers: Hold lands, remove the board before the spell resolves, and prioritize mana sources that survive land destruction. Countermagic is especially valuable because rebuilding from zero lands is often impossible under pressure.
